This petition is filed by the petitioner U/Sec 22 of Employees Compensation Act, 1923 (Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923) against respondents claiming for compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained during the course of employment with respondent No.1.
02.
The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:

That the petitioner was working under respondent No.1 as a Driver and that on 28.04.2023 at (SCCH-3) 3 E.C.A.No.49/2023 about 07.20 p.m, while he was driving the Eicher Canter bearing No.KA-05-AB-1005, opposite to Gail India Private Ltd.,
Harohalli, Bidadi Road, Medanahalli, Bidadi Hobli, Ramanagara, at that time the petitioner/driver of the said eicher canter dashed behind Tractor and Trailer bearing No.KA-42-T-6254 and KA-42-T-7390

. Consequently, the said petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and was immediately shifted to Subash Medical Centre, Bidadi, wherein after first aid treatment was given and later admitted as inpatient from 28.04.2023 to 14.05.2023 and has undergone surgery and he has spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical and conveyance expenses.
At the time of accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 32 years and earning Rs.35,000/- p.m by working as a Driver under respondent No.1.
The accident has taken place during the course and under the employment of the respondent No.1 and in this regard the Bidadi Police have registered a case.

Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- along with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
03.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appeared and hence, placed exparte.
On (SCCH-3) 4 E.C.A.No.49/2023 service of notice, respondent No.2 has appeared before this tribunal and filed objections.

04. The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and admits that this respondent has issued a policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Eicher goods vehicle bearing No.KA-53-D-9153 which was valid as on the date of accident and the liability is strictly subject to terms and conditions of the policy and further denied the alleged accident, age, avocation, income of the petitioner, nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner,
manner of accident, treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself and there is no relationship of employee and employer between the petitioner and respondent No.1 and petitioner had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the class of vehicle and there is no valid permit to the eicher canter at the time of accident and there is breach of terms and conditions of the policy and further denied that petitioner was driver by profession and working under respondent No.1 and he was not at all paid driver and the compensation claimed is (SCCH-3) 5 E.C.A.No.49/2023 exorbitant.
Hence, pray for dismiss the petition against respondent No.2 with costs.

On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues:-
ISSUES 01.
Whether the petitioner proves that he was the driver of respondent No.1 and while discharging his duty as a driver on 28.04.2023 sustained injuries as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner proves that he was the employee of respondent No.1 as on the date of alleged incident and sustained injuries during the course of employment under respondent No.1?
03. Whether the petitioner is entitled for any compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
04. What Order ?
06.
In order prove his case, the petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and got examined doctor as PW.2 and got marked 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15 and closed the petitioner side evidence.

07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 got examined its Manager Legal and FDA, RTO as RW.1 (SCCH-3) 6 E.C.A.No.49/2023 and RW.2 and got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.1 to 3 and closed its side evidence.
08. Heard both sides.

09. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 In the affirmative  Issue No.2 In the affirmative  Issue No.3
Partly
in the affirmative
Issue No.4

As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 10.

Issue Nos.1 and 2:- In order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record,
these two issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
11. The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.
Though he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2, nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.

sentences.text:
Further, PW.2 is a Doctor, who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated (SCCH-3) 7 E.C.A.No.49/2023 that the petitioner sustained fracture inter trochanteric and fracture shaft of right femur, fracture shaft of right tibia extending to articular surface (fracture proximal tibia) and he assessed total disability of right lower limb at 62% and that of his whole body at 31%
and he has produced OPD card and X-ray as per Ex.P.14 and 15 and in his cross-examination he admits that he has not given any treatment to the petitioner and he has not verified the follow-up documents and Case sheet and he has assessed the disability only and admits that both fractures are united.
Implants are not removed and there is no fracture on knee but there is fracture on hip.
There is weakness on the muscles but there is no problem for blood circulation and denied to the suggestion that he has not assess the disability of 1/3rd.

But witness voluntaries it cannot be done and that the petitioner sustained total disability of right lower limb at 62% and that of his whole body at 31% and admits that he has not assess the functional disability except physical disability and he has not issued any disability certificate and it may be less amount for future surgery for removing of implant.
13. On perusal of exhibited documents, Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR registered at Bidadi Police, against driver/petitioner of the Eicher vehicle.
Ex.P.2 is a copy (SCCH-3) 8 E.C.A.No.49/2023 of Complaint was lodged against the petitioner/driver of the Eicher vehicle.
Ex.P.3 is Spot Mahazar which shows the accident took place opposite to Gail India Private Limited, Harohalli - Bidadi Road, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.4 is IMV report which shows involvement of both vehicles in the accident.

Ex.P.5 is Charge sheet which shows that the Investigation Officer after investigation has filed Charge sheet against driver/petitioner and owner of the Eicher vehicle for the offences punishable U/Sec 279,
337, 338 of IPC and Sec.192(A) of IMV Act for the reasons that at the time of accident the eicher vehicle did not possess valid permit.
Ex.P.6 is Wound certificate shows the petitioner sustained three injuries, out of which injury Nos.1 and 2 are grievous in nature.
Ex.P.7 is Discharge summary which shows that petitioner was admitted to Subash Medical Centre as inpatient for 17 days.
Ex.P.8 is copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending Eicher canter.

Ex.P.9 is copy of Reply to notice which discloses that the owner of the offending Eicher canter has stated that the petitioner/driver was driving the said vehicle on the date of accident and he was working under him since 3 years and he caused accident to the tractor and trailer due to his rash and (SCCH-3) 9 E.C.A.No.49/2023 negligent driving and the said vehicle had RC and insurance and petitioner had a valid driving licence as on the date of accident, but no permit as on the date of accident.

14. On going through the above oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, he has proved that he was working as a Driver under respondent No.1 and he has sustained injuries in the incident on 28.04.2023 at about 07.20 p.m as alleged in the petition and it is also proved that he was the employee of respondent No.1 as on the date of accident and sustained grievous injuries during the course of employment.
Therefore, the petitioner has proved these two Issues.
Accordingly, I answered these Issues Nos.1 and 2 are in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.3:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner.

sentences.text: The petitioner in his pleading and evidence has stated that prior to the incident he was hale and healthy, aged about 32 years and earning Rs.35,000/- p.m by working as a Driver under respondent No.1 and he has spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical and conveyance.
After the accident he is not able to lead his normal life and he cannot do his avocation.
It is the duty of the petitioner to prove age, avocation and income.
But the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Ex.P.10 Aadhaar card and Ex.P.11 Driving licence.

Eventhough the said documents are not authenticated documents for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other evidence this documents can be taken into consideration and according to which the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 15.09.1991 and the alleged incident was occurred on 28.04.2023.
Therefore, considering the said documents, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 32 years.
Hence, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 32 years as on the date of alleged incident.
17. The petitioner has not produced any documents regarding his monthly income, except his driving licence and Bank statement as per Ex.P.11 and 13.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his monthly income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok- Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2023 to be taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at (SCCH-3) 11 E.C.A.No.49/2023 Rs.16,000/- and as per evidence of PW.2 doctor the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and petitioner sustained whole body disability at 31%, but he has not assessed 1/3rd of disability.
However, this tribunal has assessed the functional disability of the petitioner at 20%.

18. In order to calculate the compensation, one has to rely on Sec.4 of Employees Compensation Act,
1923.
The income of the deceased was Rs.16,000/- p.m, we have to take 60% of such amount and multiply the same with relevant factor.

The relevant factor for the age group 32 years is 203.85.
19.

Accordingly, compensation payable to the petitioner is;
Rs.16,000/-x 60% = 9,600 x 203.85 x 20% = Rs.3,91,392/-.
20. Medical expenses:-
As per Ex.P.8 Medical bills, the petitioner has incurred total medical expenses of Rs.3,18,876/-.
On perusal of Medical bills, Sl. No.1 is inpatient bill of Rs.90,550/- which is prior to discharge and Sl. No.2 is inpatient bill which is at the time of discharge.
Hence, Sl. No.1 is not considered and the said amount of Rs.90,550/- has to be deducted.
To disprove the said Medical bills, the respondent No.2 has not produced any documents nor (SCCH-3) 12 E.C.A.No.49/2023 any evidence.

Therefore, after deducting the said amount, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,28,326/-
under this head.

sentences.text: Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,19,718/- from the respondent No.2 together with interest at the rate of 12% p.a. from the date of incident till deposit of compensation amount.

22. The respondent No.2 in its objections has stated that at the time of accident the eicher vehicle had no valid permit to ply on the road and there was no employee and employer relationship between the petitioner and respondent No.1.

To disprove the said fact, the respondent No.2 got examined its Manager Legal as RW.1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has stated that the eicher canter had no valid permit to ply on the road as on the date of accident and admits issuance of policy to the said vehicle and her cross-examination nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner and she has produced Insurance Policy as per Ex.R.1 which shows that as on the date of accident the policy was valid and is in force.

23. Further, the respondent No.2 got examined FDA, Bengaluru Central RTO, as RW.2 and in his (SCCH-3) 13 E.C.A.No.49/2023 chief-examination evidence he has stated that Eicher vehicle bearing No.KA-05-AB-1005 having permit from 11.02.2016 to 10.02.2021 and it was not renewed.
As on the date of accident i.e., on 28.04.2023 there is no permit to the offending vehicle and in his cross- examination he has stated that he has not issued any notice to the respondent No.1 for renewal of permit and permit can be obtained in any other RTO Office firstly it was cancelled in his office and he has produced Permit extract as per Ex.R.3 which was valid from 11.02.2016 to 10.02.2021.
24.

The chief-evidence and cross-examination of RW.1 and RW.2 goes to show that as on the date of accident the Eicher canter had no valid permit which is evidence from Charge sheet also at Ex.P.5 and Ex.R.3 Permit extract.
25.

Therefore, considering the entire evidence on record, this tribunal is of the opinion that, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner of the Eicher canter is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and respondent No.2 Insurance Company is exonarated from the payment of compensation.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.
(SCCH-3) 14 E.C.A.No.49/2023 26. Issue No.4:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner against respondents under Sec.22 of Workmen's Compensation Act (Employees Compensation Act), 1923 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,19,718/- (Rupees Six lakhs nineteen thousand seven hundred and eighteen only) with interest at the rate of 12%
p.a from the date of incident till entire amount is deposited.

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner against respondents under Sec.22 of Workmen's Compensation Act (Employees Compensation Act), 1923 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,19,718/- (Rupees Six lakhs nineteen thousand seven hundred and eighteen only) with interest at the rate of 12%
p.a from the date of incident till entire amount is deposited.
The respondent No.1-RC Owner, shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest to the petitioner within 30 days from the date of this order.
The claim petition against respondent No.2 is hereby dismissed on without costs.

On deposit of compensation amount, petitioner is entitled to get release 75% of the award amount through E-payment directly to petitioner account by obtaining the Bank A/c details and remaining 25% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name, with a liberty to draw accrued interest.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
(SCCH-3) 15 E.C.A.No.49/2023 Draw award accordingly.
